episodes.169581: Shortwave moved through the southwesterly flow aloft that's been parked over the area this week and set off another round of severe thunderstorms over the area this afternoon into the overnight hours.  Weather pattern finally changed after the end of this event.
episodes.169594: As moisture values remained abnormally high across northern and central New Mexico on July 9, 2022, it was another busy monsoon day as numerous thunderstorms impacted the area. These thunderstorms were generally sub-severe with no flash flooding reports received, however, a strong thunderstorms with a likely wet microburst in Albuquerque produced nickel size hail and a 58 mph wind gust.
episodes.169601: Ample monsoon moisture resulted in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across western Colorado. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to localized flash flooding in Ouray County.
episodes.169902: Showers and storms accompanied a slow-moving cold front during the afternoon and evening of the 9th. A period of more persistent rain fell across southeast Bell County during the evening hours and led to a few instances of nuisance flash flooding in the Clear Fork basin of southeast Bell County.
episodes.169957: A thunderstorm became severe as it moved over the Cape in Brevard County where it produced a strong wind gust.
episodes.169958: Scattered thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in the afternoon, then pushed offshore across Brevard County. Several storms produced strong wind gusts along the Intracoastal Waterway.
episodes.170053: Disturbances moved through a persistent southwest flow aloft across the region, which continued to provide daily afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. These storms, some of which were severe, brought strong, gusty winds, severe hail, heavy localized rainfall, and lightning.
episodes.170918: Numerous severe thunderstorms occurred across the Billings Forecast Area. These thunderstorms brought large hail, along with very strong wind gusts.
episodes.170922: A thunderstorm at the Sheridan Airport produced a severe wind gust.
episodes.170923: A few thunderstorms across the southeast portions of the state produced some damaging winds and quarter size hail.
episodes.170959: Several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms worked across the Northland on the 10th with the first round moving out of Canada during the early morning hours. These storms produced localized damaging winds shortly after sunrise with a few downed trees and powerlines reported. Another round moved out of the Northern Plains across north-central Minnesota during the mid-morning hours and produced some isolated damaging winds and hail to around the size of half dollars.
episodes.170961: An area of thunderstorms develop during the afternoon hours of the 10th in association with a warm front moving into the region. While the main area of storms did not move directly over western Lake Superior, the stratiform rain on the backside of the storms did mix down a few strong wind gusts to the surface. The strongest recorded gust was 47 mph at the Port Wing harbor.
episodes.170987: A severe thunderstorm produced large hail, from quarter to golf ball size, northwest of Padroni.
episodes.171044: A broken line of thunderstorms moved through the area from the north on the evening of July 9th. These storms resulted in numerous instances of damaging winds that brought down trees and power lines mainly along and north of I-20.
episodes.171300: Isolated thunderstorms developed south of a stationary front in Central Texas and moved southward into South Central Texas. Some of these storms produced strong, damaging wind gusts.
episodes.171685: A line of thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze on the southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina coast, producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.171697: Isolated showers and thunderstorms started to develop along the sea breeze on the Charleston County coast in the early afternoon hours. A waterspout developed near Goat Island and Isle of Palms but did not produce any discernible damage. Later in the afternoon, additional thunderstorms produced gusty winds that helped bring down a few trees due to saturated soil.
episodes.171949: Above average moisture for early July combined with areawide lift from a short-wave was able to produce multiple storms capable of severe hail.
episodes.171979: Scattered storms moved across portions of northeast Iowa during the morning of July 10th. Some of these storms produced hail, with the largest reported being quarter sized in Riceville (Mitchell County).
episodes.171987: Thunderstorms developed over Montana ahead of a short-wave trough. The storms formed into a line producing primarily damaging wind gusts, and moved into western and eventually central North Dakota. Intense winds occurred with these storms, especially over the Beach and Fairfield areas where significant damage was reported. In the Beach area of Golden Valley County, estimated 90 mph wind gusts uprooted trees, damaged power lines, and damaged a few structures. Even more damage occurred in the Fairfield area of Billings County where estimated 120 mph winds broke approximately 100 power poles, blew over a two-ton transformer, blew down a communications tower, and damaged or destroyed some structures. A few of the storms produced large hail, the largest being golf ball size, and occurred near Heart Butte Dam in Grant County.
episodes.172009: A late season cold front pushed southward across Central Alabama on July 9th.  The air mass ahead of the front was very unstable with afternoon surface based CAPE of 4000-4500 J/kg and lifted indices around -7 Celsius.  PWAT's were above two inches which also supported heavy rainfall and flash flooding.
episodes.172021: A strong thunderstorm moved across Saxon Harbor during the evening of the 10th.
episodes.172155: An induced surface trough and a tropical wave approaches the islands. At the same time, an upper level trough dug from the northeast, providing instability aloft. The combination of these features resulted in periods of heavy rain and gusty winds, with multiple flooding reports received.
episodes.172170: A weak frontal boundary which sagged south through the I-20 corridor provided focus for isolated thunderstorm development on the afternoon of Saturday July 9. Triple digit temperatures that afternoon provided sufficient instability for severe downburst winds in a few of these storms.
episodes.172313: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced strong winds.
episodes.172371: Isolated late afternoon thunderstorms developed across the Concho Valley and Heartland due to moderate instability and hot temperatures. A few storms were severe and caused wind damage and hail.
episodes.172505: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots as well as a few sightings of waterspouts.
episodes.172601: A very warm and humid air mass south of an approaching backdoor front combined with passing mid level disturbances within a broad mid-level trough to produce widespread showers and storms. Very high moisture, deeply warm low levels, and slow storm motion produced high rainfall rates and flash flooding, ranging from nuisance flooding in most places to road closures in Chapel Hill, Durham, and Wake county. Isolated damaging winds were also reported in Sampson County.
episodes.172631: Scattered showers and thunderstorms associated with low pressure moving along a frontal boundary produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of the Virginia Northern Neck and Middle Peninsula.
episodes.172639: An area of 1 to 2 inches of rainfall occurred across the headwaters of the Little Sioux River on July 5 and resulted in a brief period of minor to locally moderate flooding.
episodes.172655: Severe thunderstorms impacted the region through the morning, midday, and early afternoon hours. Damaging wind gusts were the primary threat through the morning, with increasing reports of hail heading into the midday and afternoon.
episodes.172656: Severe thunderstorms impacted the region through the morning, midday, and early afternoon hours. Damaging wind gusts were the primary threat through the morning, with increasing reports of hail heading into the midday and afternoon.
episodes.172779: Slow moving thunderstorms caused very heavy rain across portions oof northwest that created some flooding.
episodes.172786: A slow-moving cold front was a focus of convective development that led to flash flooding.

On the evening of July 9, 2022, a cluster of thunderstorms was moving southeast across northern Hinds County. At approximately 9:39 PM CDT, a segment of the thunderstorm cluster resulted in rapidly intensifying winds at ground level. Damage from this corridor of enhanced wind, estimated to have maximum gusts to 80 mph, impacted initially near areas of the Castlewoods Country club near Castlewoods Boulevard, spreading outward primarily to the southeast. The damage across the area consisted primarily of trees down of varying varieties, some large. The most intense damage occurred near the golf course on the southeastern side of Castlewoods where numerous large pines were felled. Several homes in this area had minor to moderate gutter/siding damage along with numerous wooden fence segments blown over. Damage was noted to be divergent in nature, providing confidence in the straight-line wind nature of this event, from what was a likely downburst with rapidly descending winds that spread out upon reaching the surface. The corridor of damage continued east spreading out along highway 471 and southeast to just north of Grants Ferry Road with progressive reductions in damage, ending just beyond the highway where only small branches down and vegetative debris was found.

Shortly after midnight on July 10th, an intense microburst occurred around Grand Gulf in Clairborne county. This swath of damage started at the MS River near the Military Park and pushed south southeast to southeast and moved over the Grand Gulf Nuclear facility. Damage from this microburst was primarily in the form of uprooted or broken trees. Several hundred trees were damaged. Additionally, several power lines and poles were taken down. There was one camper that had a large tree through it. Several roads were blocked or blocked in multiple locations in this area. Roads that were blocked included Grand Gulf Road, Back Grand Gulf Road, Frazier Road and Bald Hill Road. Damage was consistent with peak winds in the 70-85 mph range. The damage swath was almost 5 miles long and rough 3.5 miles wide.
